To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GSH is the key determinant of the redox-dependent mechanism of action of bioreducible liposomes for gene delivery.
GSH is a major determinant of transfection efficiency of redox-sensitive vectors.

1) the presence of diooleoyl chains and ethanolamine headgroups in co-lipid composition of bioreducible liposomes significantly improved transfection efficiency of the corresponding liposomes; 2) intracellular GSH concentration, but not the oxidative stress, is the main driver of transfection of biodegradable lipoplexes; 3) GSH is the main driver in the transfection process of bioreducible systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of redox-sensitive cationic liposomes with improved transfection efficiencies.
the formulation of a bioreducible liposome for gene delivery and with the identification of the determinants of the transfection efficiency.
the formulation, the characterization and the mechanistic investigation of SS14 redoxy-sensitive gemini surfacant for gene delivery into cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSH is the major player in the mechanism of action of SS14 lipoplexes, and that the redox milieu, rather than GSH alone, is the key determinant for DNA release in vitro and transfection in cells.
the redox milieu of the intracellular environment is the main driving force for DNA release in bioreducible transfection.
the redox gradient across the plasma membrane is the main driving force of gene release and transfection efficiency of SS14 bioreducible lipoplexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intracellular reducing environment, and not oxidative stress, is a determinant factor in the transfection efficiency of redox-responsive lipoplexes.

the presence of GSH in its whole is essential for transfection of biodegradable lipoplexes, and that the presence of dioleyl chains and PE head groups in co-cationic lipids are essential to improve transfection efficiencies of bioreducible lipoplexes.
bioreducible liposomes are a promising strategy for gene therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GSH is a key factor to consider for the rational development of bioreducible gene delivery systems.
the redox gradient is a key determinant in gene transfection of biodegradable vectors.
bioreductive transfectants may be designed and tailored to exploit GSH as a trigger to release DNA into the cell.
